# Includes {#includes}

An include directive is a block of its own: there is no inline include, and the line below a directive starts a new block (C2-N-002, C2-B-156). Ids are not renamed across files and footnote labels resolve per file (C2-N-055, C2-N-057).

**U-011** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> Include directive
Tool: Review by hand.

::: compare no-render
```text
Some text
{{ other.crv }}
```
```html
<p>Some text
{{ other.crv }}</p>
```
:::

**U-184** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> A line below an include directive starts a block of its own under C2-B-156, also a second directive
Tool: Review by hand: - <span v-pre>\{{</span> e }} ⏎   b keeps the 0.1 HTML only where no resolver is given.

::: compare no-render
```text
- {{ e }}
  b
```
<!-- carve-sample {"lint":"unattached-inline-attribute reports the brace block after the escaped brace of the map spelling; carve-js next2 b967be5 keeps the include as written"} -->
```crv
- \{{ e }}
  b
```
:::

**U-289** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-H-133 and C2-N-070, a social token inside an unexpanded include: <code v-pre>{{ a.crv @shift:1 }}</code> with no resolver, <code v-pre>{{ part.crv @unknown:foo }}</code> with one
Tool: The directive is text, <code v-pre>&lt;p&gt;{{ a.crv @shift:1 }}&lt;/p&gt;</code>. Escaping the opening brace gives the 0.1 HTML but stops the include from being expanded where a resolver is given.

::: compare no-render
```text
{{ a.crv @shift:1 }}
```
```text
<p>{{ a.crv @shift:1 }}</p> An unexpanded include renders the directive as text (C2-H-133, C2-N-070), so no inline form is read in it; with no resolver, or with an invalid option such as `@unknown:foo` under a resolver, 0.1 read `@shift` as a mention, `<span class="mention"><strong>@shift</strong></span>`. Escaping the opening brace gives the 0.1 HTML but makes the line text that no resolver expands, so the row is a report.
```
:::

**U-290** <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-N-002, a directive with an invalid option inside a sentence: <code v-pre>x {{ a.crv @lines:0 }} y</code>

::: compare no-render
```text
x {{ a.crv @lines:0 }} y
```
```crv
x {{ a.crv \@lines:0 }} y
```
:::

**U-291** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-H-133 and C2-H-171, an unexpanded include with an option glued to the path or options in another order: <code v-pre>{{ a.crv@code:js }}</code>, `@cols` before `@code`
Tool: Written from the tree: <code v-pre>{{ a.crv @code:js }}</code>, each option after one space in the order of C2-W-058. No 0.2 source keeps the authored spelling.

::: compare no-render
```text
{{ a.crv@code:js }}
```
```text
<p>{{ a.crv @code:js }}</p> An unexpanded include writes the directive from the tree, each option after one space and in the order of C2-W-058 (C2-H-133, C2-H-171); 0.1 wrote the source as authored, `{{ a.crv@code:js }}`, and kept the authored order of `@code` and `@cols`. No 0.2 source writes the glued spelling.
```
:::

**U-292** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-N-072, attributes on an unexpanded include: `{.diff}` above <code v-pre>{{ a.crv @code:js }}</code> with no resolver; `{table}` above a table include rejected for `@rows:0-2`
Tool: An include's own attributes are never written: <code v-pre>&lt;p&gt;{{ a.crv @code:js }}&lt;/p&gt;</code>. The caption of a code include is another matter.

::: compare no-render
```text
{.diff}
{{ a.crv @code:js }}
```
```text
<p>{{ a.crv @code:js }}</p> An include's own attributes are not written to HTML (C2-N-072, C2-A-181), so the fallback paragraph of an unexpanded include has none; 0.1 wrote them on it, `<p class="diff">`, also the `{table}` key on a table include rejected for an invalid `@rows`. The caption of a code include is not part of this row.
```
:::

**U-301** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-N-020, a line or region selection whose first line is a `---` line, <code v-pre>{{ a.crv @lines:3-7 }}</code> on an `a.crv` of `x`, a blank line, `---`, `t: 1`, `---`, a blank line and `para`, opened frontmatter in 0.1: `<p>para</p>`.
Tool: Start the selection below the closing `---` line.

::: compare no-render
```text
{{ a.crv @lines:3-7 }}
```
```text
<p>—
t: 1
—</p>
<p>para</p> for an `a.crv` of `x`, a blank line, `---`, `t: 1`, `---`, a blank line and `para`. C2-N-020: a selection opens frontmatter only when it starts at line 1 of the file; 0.1 read the selected `---` lines as frontmatter and wrote <p>para</p>. Start the selection below the closing `---` line where the lines are meant as frontmatter.
```
:::

**U-302** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-N-020 and C2-N-054, a line or region selection resolved its references only against the definitions it selected in 0.1: <code v-pre>{{ a.crv @region:k }}</code> on a region that holds `See [s][] and HTML.`, with `[s]: /u` and `*[HTML]: Hyper` below it, wrote `[s][]` and a plain `HTML`.
Tool: Review references in the selected lines.

::: compare no-render
```text
{{ a.crv @region:k }}
```
```text
<p>See <a href="/u">s</a> and <abbr title="Hyper">HTML</abbr>.</p> for an `a.crv` of `%% #region k`, `See [s][] and HTML.`, `%% #endregion k`, a blank line, `[s]: /u` and `*[HTML]: Hyper`. C2-N-020, C2-N-054: a line or region selection sees every definition of its file, as a section does (C2-N-031); 0.1 resolved only against the selected lines and wrote <p>See [s][] and HTML.</p>.
```
:::
